cluster_name: Michigan reports first two deaths in US Cyclospora outbreak
tldr: The headline layer is overwhelmingly locked on a single HEALTH_SAFETY milestone framing — first US deaths in the cyclospora outbreak — with near-identical wording across all 11 geographic buckets. The one substantive headline divergence is tonal rather than factual: BBC World, France Info, The Independent, and one Hindustan Times article all use vivid symptom language ('explosive diarrhoea / diarrhées explosives / explosive diarrhea'), while wire-service and neutral outlets favour 'cyclosporiasis' or 'diarrhea-causing parasite.' Daily Wire abandons pathogen-first framing entirely, naming the story by food vector ('lettuce outbreak') and using dramatising language ('deadly turn'). The record-breaking scale of the outbreak (18,000+ cases), the CDC's investigative uncertainty, and Taylor Farms de Mexico's supply-chain role — all prominent in body text — are completely invisible in every homepage headline.
event_summary: Two people died in Michigan from Cyclospora on August 4, 2026, the first US fatalities in a multistate outbreak of over 18,000 cases ongoing since May.

single_outlet_findings.finding: The only headline to name the food vector ('The Lettuce Outbreak') rather than the pathogen or the Michigan milestone, and to use dramatising language ('Just Took A Deadly Turn') — converting the epidemiological story into a food-crisis narrative at homepage level.

The only outlet to surface a reader-advisory angle in the headline itself ('know symptoms, how to stay safe and more'), adding a POLICY_PRESCRIPTION register to the milestone framing that no other headline in the corpus signals.

bottom_line: At the headline layer, all 11 geographic buckets converge on a single HEALTH_SAFETY milestone — first deaths in the cyclospora outbreak — with variation confined to whether outlets used visceral symptom language ('explosive diarrhea/diarrhoea') or neutral clinical terms ('cyclosporiasis'). The record-breaking outbreak scale, the CDC's investigative uncertainty, and the implicated Mexican food supplier — all prominent in body text — are entirely absent from every homepage headline.
